mainTopic: Mourning laws for young children, counting mourning days around the festivals, and a new משנה on tearing garments and the mourner's meal
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא about babies who die. It explains how they are carried out for burial and which mourning customs apply at each age. Under thirty days there is no שורה, ברכת אבלים, or תנחומי אבלים. From thirty days a small coffin is used and these customs are done. A twelve-month-old goes out on a מטה, but רבי עקיבא limits this to a child with the age or body size of a two-year-old. Two תנאים then give tests for public involvement, and the ברייתא sets the age at which a child gets a הספד. רב rules like רבי יהודה's version: from five for the poor and the elderly, and from six for the wealthy. Next the גמרא teaches that one day of mourning before עצרת plus עצרת count as fourteen days toward the שלושים. Sages objected when this was taught without naming its source, רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא, who learns from a פסוק that עצרת is like a seven-day festival. The count is extended to ראש השנה (only according to רבן גמליאל, as רבינא explains) and to סוכות with שמיני עצרת, which make twenty-one days. A new משנה then begins about who tears garments and is served the mourner's first meal during the festival.

steps.title: אבא שאול allows one man and two women to bury a young infant
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול disagrees with the first opinion and allows a very young baby to be buried even by one man and two women.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: The baby may be taken out and buried even by one man and two women.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא about burying a baby less than thirty days old. אבא שאול gives his own opinion about who may handle the burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinion said only one woman and two men, but not one man and two women, which reflects a concern about יחוד (being alone together). אבא שאול says 'even' one man and two women, so he does not worry about that here. The reason usually given is that at a time of mourning people are not drawn to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Even; it widens the earlier rule

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers a statement that comes just before this section. The first opinion forbade one man and two women. אבא שאול's 'even' only makes sense against that background.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
Even with one man and two women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the earlier line of the ברייתא (just before this section) that allowed only one woman and two men.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אבא שאול, one man and two women may bury a baby under thirty days old.

steps.title: No formal mourning customs for a very young infant
steps.stepSummary: For a baby under thirty days, people do not stand in a line, and they do not say the mourners' blessing or the formal words of comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people do not stand in a line for him, and they do not say for him the mourners' blessing or the comforting of mourners.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists three public mourning customs that are NOT done for a baby who died before thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally after a burial, people form a line (שורה) to comfort the mourners. A ברכת אבלים is said, and during the week people say תנחומי אבלים. For such a young baby, none of these formal public steps are done. This sets up a contrast with the thirty-day-old baby in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A line of people who comfort the mourners after the burial
The mourners' blessing said after a burial

phrases.english: And they do not stand for him in a line.
And they do not say over him the mourners' blessing
Or the comforting of mourners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עוֹמְדִין עָלָיו בְּשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's rules for a baby under thirty days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a baby under thirty days, people do not stand in a line, and they do not say ברכת אבלים or תנחומי אבלים.

steps.title: A thirty-day-old infant is carried in a small coffin
steps.stepSummary: A thirty-day-old baby is taken out in a small coffin. רבי יהודה says it should be a coffin carried in the arms, not one carried on the shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thirty-day-old baby is taken out in a small coffin. רבי יהודה says: Not a coffin carried on the shoulder, but one carried in the arms.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves up one age level, to a baby of thirty days. רבי יהודה clarifies which kind of small coffin is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby under thirty days is carried in someone's arms with no coffin. At thirty days, a דלוסקמא (small coffin) is used, which is more formal. רבי יהודה says it should be carried in the arms of two people, not on one person's shoulder. That makes the procession more like a real funeral.

phrases.english: A thirty-day-old is taken out in a coffin.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not a coffin that is carried on the shoulder,
But rather one that is carried in the arms.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹצֵא בִּדְלוֹסְקָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the under-thirty-day baby to the thirty-day-old baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thirty-day-old baby goes out in a small coffin. רבי יהודה says it is carried in the arms, not on the shoulder.

steps.title: Full mourning customs for a thirty-day-old infant
steps.stepSummary: For a thirty-day-old baby, people do stand in a line, and they say the mourners' blessing and the comforting of mourners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And people stand in a line for him, and they say for him the mourners' blessing and the comforting of mourners.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says that the three customs NOT done for a younger baby ARE done for a thirty-day-old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These lines mirror step 2 almost word for word, but without the word 'not'. This shows that thirty days is the turning point. From thirty days on, the baby gets the public mourning customs that an older person gets.
steps.whatToRemember: Thirty days is the dividing line. Under thirty days there is no שורה, ברכת אבלים, or תנחומי אבלים. From thirty days on, all three are done.

phrases.english: And they stand for him in a line,
And they say over him the mourners' blessing
And the comforting of mourners.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹמְדִין עָלָיו בְּשׁוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite of step 2 for the older, thirty-day-old baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a thirty-day-old baby, people stand in a שורה and say ברכת אבלים and תנחומי אבלים.

steps.title: A twelve-month-old is carried on a regular bier
steps.stepSummary: A twelve-month-old baby goes out on a bier like an adult. רבי עקיבא limits this: the child goes out on a bier only if he has either the age or the body size of a two-year-old.
steps.simpleTranslation: A twelve-month-old baby is taken out on a bier. רבי עקיבא says: If he is one year old but his limbs look like a two-year-old's, or he is two years old but his limbs look like a one-year-old's, he is taken out on a bier.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reaches the next age level, a baby of twelve months, who is carried on a full bier. רבי עקיבא then talks about babies whose size does not match their age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bier (מטה) is what adults are carried on, so the first opinion gives a twelve-month-old an adult-style funeral. רבי עקיבא narrows this: a bier is used only if the child has the age of a two-year-old or the body size of one. A plain one-year-old with ordinary-sized limbs does not go out on a bier.

keyTerms.meaning: A bier, the stretcher used to carry an adult who has died
His limbs, meaning his body size

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ יוֹצֵא בְּמִטָּה.
phrases.english: A twelve-month-old is taken out on a bier.
Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בֶּן שָׁנָה וְאֵבָרָיו כְּבֶן שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: If he is one year old and his limbs are like a two-year-old's,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בֶּן שְׁתַּיִם וְאֵבָרָיו כְּבֶן שָׁנָה —
phrases.english: Or he is two years old and his limbs are like a one-year-old's —
He is taken out on a bier.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (רבי עקיבא's part could be read as a narrowing of the first rule)
steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ יוֹצֵא בְּמִטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the thirty-day-old to the twelve-month-old.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first opinion, a twelve-month-old goes out on a מטה. רבי עקיבא requires the child to have either the age or the body size of a two-year-old.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the public grieves for a child carried on a bier
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the public must grieve for a child who goes out on a bier, but not for one who does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: For a child who goes out on a bier, the public grieves. For one who does not go out on a bier, the public does not grieve.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא gives a general rule for when the wider community must take part in the mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a list of ages, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר links public mourning to the bier from step 5. If the child is old enough to go out on a מטה, the public mourns. If not, the mourning stays with the family.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
One who is taken out on a bier —
The public grieves over him.
One who is not taken out on a bier —
The public does not grieve over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: הַיּוֹצֵא בְּמִטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a general rule about public mourning on the bier mentioned in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public grieves only for a child who goes out on a מטה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: it depends on whether the public knew the child
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the public takes part in the burial if the child was known to the public, and not otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: If the child was known to the public, the public takes part in his burial. If he was not known to the public, the public does not take part.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא offers a different general rule. He bases public involvement on whether people knew the child, not on age or the bier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה looks at the child's place in the community. If the child went out and many people knew him, the public must get involved. If he was not known, the public does not have to. This is a separate standard from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's bier test.

keyTerms.meaning: Take care of him, take part in his burial

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends with two different tests for public involvement. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר asks whether the child goes out on a מטה. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה asks whether the child was known to the public.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
If he was known to the public —
The public occupies itself with him,
If he was not known to the public —
The public does not occupy itself with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: נִיכָּר לָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different test from step 6 for when the public must get involved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The public takes part in a child's burial only if the child was known to the public.

steps.title: From what age a child gets a eulogy: the first view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks when a young child gets a הספד. רבי מאיר, quoting רבי ישמעאל, says children of the poor from age three and children of the wealthy from age five.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is their status regarding a eulogy? רבי מאיר says in the name of רבי ישמעאל: children of the poor are eulogized from age three, and children of the wealthy from age five.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from burial rules to a new question: from what age do we give a הספד for a child who died? It gives the first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age depends on whether the family is poor or wealthy. A poor family's children get a הספד at a younger age. The usual reason given is that a child is a poor family's main joy, so their grief is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: A eulogy; a public speech of mourning for the one who died
In the name of; quoting someone else

phrases.english: And what is their status regarding a eulogy?
phrases.notes: "Their" means the young children the ברייתא has been talking about in the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
The poor: from age three,
The wealthy: from age five.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הֵן בְּהֶסְפֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about deceased children, moving from burial practice to the age at which a child gets a הספד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר's version of רבי ישמעאל: children of the poor get a הספד from age three, children of the wealthy from age five.

steps.title: A second version of the same opinion, with older ages
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה quotes רבי ישמעאל differently: the poor from age five, the wealthy from age six, and children of elderly parents are treated like children of the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in his name: children of the poor from age five, children of the wealthy from age six, and children of elderly parents are like children of the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה reports a different version of what רבי ישמעאל said. He gives older ages and adds a rule for elderly parents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages agree that the poor get the lower age. They only disagree about which ages רבי ישמעאל actually said. רבי יהודה adds that elderly parents get the lower age too, like poor families.

keyTerms.meaning: In his name; here, quoting רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion of רבי יהודה himself. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are both reporting what רבי ישמעאל said, and they remember it differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name:
phrases.notes: "His name" means רבי ישמעאל, the same sage רבי מאיר quoted.

phrases.english: The poor: from age five,
The wealthy: from age six,
And children of the elderly are like children of the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשְּׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing report of רבי ישמעאל's opinion from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה's version: the poor from age five, the wealthy from age six, and the elderly are treated like the poor.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל בר מנשיא reports that רב ruled like רבי יהודה's report of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל בר מנשיא said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who spoke in the name of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא decides between the two versions from steps 8 and 9. We follow רבי יהודה's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, children of the poor and of elderly parents get a הספד from age five, and children of the wealthy from age six. This closes the discussion of the ages.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a child gets a הספד from age five in a poor or elderly family, and from age six in a wealthy family.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Giddel bar Menashya said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda,
who spoke in the name of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement between the two versions in steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Practical law follows רבי יהודה's version of רבי ישמעאל's ages.

steps.title: One day before עצרת plus עצרת count as fourteen days
steps.stepSummary: רבי ענני בר ששון publicly teaches that a mourner who mourned one day before עצרת has fourteen days counted toward his mourning once עצרת is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ענני בר ששון taught at the entrance of the נשיא's house: one day before עצרת, and עצרת itself, make fourteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: mourning that runs into the holiday of עצרת (שבועות). It brings a public teaching about how to count the days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual explanation: one day of mourning before the holiday counts as the full שבעה, because the holiday ends the שבעה. עצרת then counts as seven more days, like the other holidays, even though it is only one day. That makes fourteen days toward the thirty-day שלושים.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, gave a public lecture
The house of the נשיא, the leader of the Jewish community

steps.whyThisMatters: It tells a mourner how much of the שלושים is left after עצרת. Only sixteen days remain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Anani bar Sason taught publicly
at the entrance of the house of the Nasi:
One day before Atzeret, and Atzeret,
here are fourteen days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן אַפִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: counting mourning days around עצרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day of mourning before עצרת plus עצרת itself count as fourteen days of mourning.

steps.title: רבי אמי objects: the teaching was not given in its author's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי hears the teaching and gets upset. It is not רבי ענני's own idea; it was said by רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי heard and became angry. He said: Is it his own teaching? It is the teaching that רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי does not argue with the law itself. He objects that רבי ענני taught it as if it were his own, without naming who really said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling of fourteen days stays the same. The complaint is only about credit. The real source is רבי אלעזר quoting רבי אושעיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that...? (a word that opens a complaint)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי agrees with the law. He is only upset that the teaching was not said in the name of the sage who first taught it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami heard and became angry,
He said: Is it his own teaching?

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא הִיא!
phrases.english: It is what Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ דִּידֵיהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to how step 11's teaching was presented, not to its content.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי ענני בר ששון presented the teaching, with no name attached.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching really belongs to רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא, so teaching it without naming them is improper.

steps.title: The same teaching given again in the ראש גלותא's hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא publicly teaches the same rule: one day before עצרת plus עצרת make fourteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא taught in the hall of the ראש גלותא: one day before עצרת, and עצרת itself, make fourteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, almost identical story. Another sage teaches the same rule in a different place, and this sets up a second objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law is exactly the same as in step 11. What is new is the speaker and the place. This shows the teaching spread in more than one place without its source being named.

keyTerms.meaning: The ראש גלותא, the leader of the Jews in Babylonia

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha taught publicly
in the hall of the Reish Galuta:
One day before Atzeret, and Atzeret,
here are fourteen days.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אַקִּילְעָא דְּרֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the teaching of step 11 in a parallel story with a different speaker and place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day of mourning before עצרת plus עצרת itself count as fourteen days.

steps.title: רב ששת makes the same objection
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת hears it and is upset in the same way: the teaching belongs to רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת heard and became angry. He said: Is it his own teaching? It is the teaching that רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא!
steps.whatsHappening: Just like רבי אמי in step 12, רב ששת objects that the teaching was not credited to its true source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, no one disputes the law of fourteen days. Two separate sages insisting on the same point shows how much it matters to name the source of a teaching.
steps.whatToRemember: One day of mourning before עצרת plus עצרת count as fourteen days. The teaching comes from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא, and the sages insisted it be quoted in their name.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet heard and became angry,
He said: Is it his own teaching?

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא הִיא!
phrases.english: It is what Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ דִּידֵיהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats step 12's objection, this time against step 13's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי יצחק נפחא presented the teaching, with no name attached.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching belongs to רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא and should have been quoted in their name.

steps.title: The original source: עצרת has make-up days for all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא: עצרת has seven days to make up its offerings, just like פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: How do we know that עצרת has make-up days for all seven days? Because the פסוק says 'בחג המצות ובחג השבועות.' Just as חג המצות has make-up days for all seven, so too חג השבועות has make-up days for all seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי אמי and רב ששת were upset. The 'fourteen days' idea comes from this teaching of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places פסח and שבועות side by side, so the גמרא learns one from the other. פסח lasts seven days, so שבועות also gets seven days to make up its offerings. Because עצרת is treated like a seven-day festival, it counts as seven days toward the thirty days of mourning, which is how steps 11 and 13 reach fourteen.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up time for bringing a festival offering that was missed on the day itself

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that turns the one-day festival of עצרת into a 'seven-day' festival for mourning purposes. That is the basis for the fourteen-day count.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
From where do we know that Shavuot
has make-up days for all seven days?
phrases.notes: If someone missed bringing his festival offering on שבועות itself, he can still bring it during the next six days.

phrases.english: As it says:
"On the festival of matzos and on the festival of Shavuot"
Just as the festival of matzos
has make-up days for all seven,
so too the festival of Shavuot
has make-up days for all seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the complaint of steps 12 and 14 by quoting the original teaching and its source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עצרת has make-up days for its offerings for all seven days, learned from פסח. So it counts as a seven-day festival.

steps.title: Applying the count to ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא סבא, given the floor by רב פפא, teaches that one day before ראש השנה plus ראש השנה make fourteen days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא had רב אויא סבא speak, and he taught publicly: One day of mourning before ראש השנה, plus ראש השנה, make fourteen days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new public teaching applies the same counting idea to ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One day of mourning before the holiday cancels the שבעה, which counts as seven days. ראש השנה then counts as another seven, just like עצרת did. Together that makes fourteen days toward the thirty-day mourning period.

keyTerms.meaning: He led him / gave him the floor to speak

phrases.aramaic: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרַב אַוְיָא סָבָא
phrases.english: Rav Pappa led Rav Avya the Elder [to speak]
and he taught publicly:
One day before Rosh Hashana
and Rosh Hashana
here are fourteen [days].

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרַב אַוְיָא סָבָא וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the fourteen-day count of עצרת and applies it to ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day of mourning before ראש השנה, plus ראש השנה, count as fourteen days.

steps.title: Extending the count to סוכות and שמיני עצרת
steps.stepSummary: רבינא concludes that one day before סוכות, plus סוכות, plus שמיני עצרת, make twenty-one days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Therefore, one day before the festival, plus the festival, plus its eighth day, make twenty-one days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא builds on the previous teaching and applies the same logic to סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count works like this: the day before the festival cancels the שבעה (7), סוכות counts as 7 more (14), and שמיני עצרת counts as its own festival worth 7 (21). So only nine days of mourning are left to complete thirty.

keyTerms.meaning: Its eighth day, meaning שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: Ravina said: Therefore:
One day before the festival,
and the festival, and its eighth day,
here are twenty-one days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a further conclusion from the same counting method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One day before סוכות, plus סוכות, plus שמיני עצרת, count as twenty-one days.

steps.title: רב חביבא asks רבינא about the ראש השנה rule
steps.stepSummary: In סורא דפרת, רב חביבא asks רבינא whether he really said that one day before ראש השנה plus ראש השנה make fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came to סורא on the Euphrates. רב חביבא of סורא on the Euphrates said to רבינא: Did the master say that one day before ראש השנה plus ראש השנה make fourteen?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone checks with רבינא whether the ראש השנה rule is really his ruling. This sets up רבינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראש השנה rule is not obvious, because ראש השנה is not one of the three pilgrimage festivals. רב חביבא wants to know whether רבינא truly holds it as the הלכה.

phrases.english: Ravina happened to come to Sura on the Euphrates.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חֲבִיבָא מִסּוּרָא דִפְרָת לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chaviva from Sura on the Euphrates said to Ravina:
Did the master say:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: one day before Rosh Hashana and Rosh Hashana
here are fourteen?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, יוֹם אֶחָד לִפְנֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הֲרֵי כָּאן אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the ראש השנה rule is really a practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבינא actually rule that ראש השנה counts as seven days for mourning?

steps.title: רבינא: I only said it is logical according to רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that he only said the ראש השנה count makes sense according to רבן גמליאל, not that it is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What I said was only that it stands to reason according to רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question and narrows his statement. He was only explaining one opinion, not giving a final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that ראש השנה and יום הכפורים are like the festivals for mourning purposes, as in the earlier משנה. According to him, the fourteen-day count makes sense. רבינא is not saying the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason / it is logical

steps.whatToRemember: The fourteen-day count for ראש השנה only works according to רבן גמליאל. רבינא did not rule that way as the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבינא as agreeing with the ראש השנה rule. He only said that it fits רבן גמליאל's opinion.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I, 'it stands to reason according to Rabban Gamliel,'
is what I said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא, מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הוּא דְּאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חביבא's question by limiting the statement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ראש השנה count is only a logical explanation of רבן גמליאל's view, not a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ראש השנה count depends on רבן גמליאל and is not the accepted הלכה.

steps.title: New משנה: who tears garments and how the mourner's meal is served
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that only close relatives of the deceased tear garments, bare the shoulder, and are served the mourner's first meal, and that this meal is served only on an upright bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: They do not tear garments, do not bare the shoulder, and do not serve the mourner's first meal, except for the close relatives of the deceased. And they serve the first meal only on an upright bed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing mourning practices that are limited during the festival time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing, baring the shoulder, and the mourner's first meal are kept only for the actual close relatives. The meal is served while the mourner sits on an upright bed, not an overturned one, because during the festival time the bed is not turned over.

keyTerms.meaning: Baring the shoulder by pulling off the garment
Serving the mourner's first meal after the burial

phrases.english: MISHNA: They do not tear [garments] and do not bare [the shoulder]
and they do not serve the mourner's first meal,
except for the close relatives of the deceased.
And they do not serve the first meal
except on an upright bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין קוֹרְעִין וְלֹא חוֹלְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tearing, baring the shoulder, and the mourner's first meal apply only to the close relatives of the deceased, and the meal is served only on an upright bed.
